Title: The Deepest Water
QuestionDetail: The Mariana Trench, the deepest known point in any ocean, lies in which ocean?
AnswerDetails: The Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench, sits roughly 11,000 metres below the surface - deeper than Mount Everest is tall.
CustomInstruction: Picture where the trench sits relative to the Philippines and Guam before you look at the options.

Title: The Deepest Lake
QuestionDetail: Lake Baikal, the deepest freshwater lake on Earth, lies in which country?
AnswerDetails: Lake Baikal in southern Siberia reaches about 1,640 metres deep and holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.
CustomInstruction: Deep matters here, not large. Rule out the options by continent first.

Title: Everest's Other Side
QuestionDetail: Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and which other country?
AnswerDetails: The summit lies on the Nepal-China border; the northern approach runs through the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
CustomInstruction: Two of these options border Nepal. Decide which one the summit itself actually touches.

Title: Mostly Not Oxygen
QuestionDetail: Which gas makes up roughly 78 percent of Earth's atmosphere?
AnswerDetails: Nitrogen accounts for about 78 percent of dry air by volume, with oxygen at about 21 percent and argon making up most of the remainder.
CustomInstruction: The intuitive answer is the one we breathe for. Trust the number, not the intuition.

Title: Three Hundred Thousand What?
QuestionDetail: In a vacuum, light travels at approximately 300,000 of which unit per second?
AnswerDetails: The speed of light in a vacuum is 299,792,458 metres per second, which is very close to 300,000 kilometres per second.
CustomInstruction: Work from the number rather than the memory of the phrase. Which unit makes 300,000 the right order of magnitude?

Title: Top of the Scale
QuestionDetail: On the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, which mineral scores the maximum value of 10?
AnswerDetails: The Mohs scale runs from talc at 1 to diamond at 10. Corundum, which includes rubies and sapphires, sits just below at 9.
CustomInstruction: One of these is famously second-hardest. Make sure you are not picking the runner-up.

Title: Reads Both Ways
QuestionDetail: Which of these words is a palindrome - identical read forwards and backwards?
AnswerDetails: A palindrome reads the same in both directions. Level reverses to level; the others do not.
CustomInstruction: Spell each option backwards in your head before choosing. Three of them are near misses on purpose.

Title: A Word for a Wave
QuestionDetail: The English word tsunami is borrowed from which language?
AnswerDetails: Tsunami comes from Japanese, combining the words for harbour and wave - a name given by coastal communities who saw the effect in port.
CustomInstruction: Think about the literal meaning of the word - harbour wave - and which coastal culture would have coined it.

Title: Coined in a Play
QuestionDetail: The word robot entered English from a 1920 stage play by Karel Capek. Which language did it come from?
AnswerDetails: Capek's play R.U.R. introduced the word, adapted from a Slavic root meaning forced labour. Capek credited his brother Josef with the coinage.
CustomInstruction: The playwright's nationality is the answer. If the name is unfamiliar, work from the root meaning forced labour.

Title: Where the Web Began
QuestionDetail: The World Wide Web was proposed in 1989 by Tim Berners-Lee while he was working at which organisation?
AnswerDetails: Berners-Lee wrote his proposal at CERN, the particle physics laboratory near Geneva, to help researchers share documents across incompatible systems.
CustomInstruction: Three of these are famous for computing. The answer is famous for something else entirely.

Title: Movable Type
QuestionDetail: Around 1440 Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing to Europe. He worked in a city in which modern-day country?
AnswerDetails: Gutenberg worked in Mainz, in present-day Germany. Movable type had existed earlier in East Asia; his contribution was a practical metal-type press for European scripts.
CustomInstruction: The city was Mainz. Place it on a map and the country follows.

Title: The Key to a Script
QuestionDetail: The Rosetta Stone was the crucial aid in deciphering which writing system?
AnswerDetails: The stone carries the same decree in Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic script and ancient Greek, letting scholars use the Greek to unlock the hieroglyphs.
CustomInstruction: The stone's value came from a script scholars could already read sitting beside one they could not. Which pair does that describe?
